how_these_were_chosen: The spec's arm A1 requires 'w3's seed plus one new', because world-holding is a scene claim and a scene claim needs two seeds. So the first number is E11 wave 3's own seed, carried deliberately, and the second continues the date-plus-index rule the arc has used all day: 2026-08-12, run 41.

allocation.2026081233: seed 1 — E11 wave 3's seed, REUSED on purpose. w3 ran it on the same weights, the same 1024x576x81 frame, the same trajectory and the same prompt, differing only in the start frame. Holding the seed makes that one difference the only difference, which is what the ladder is for.
allocation.2026081241: seed 2 — a number this experiment has never run, so the world claim is not read off a single noise field.

why_reusing_a_seed_from_another_experime: specs/E11-seeds.json states that reusing a registered number across experiments leaves the record having to explain which run a number belonged to. That objection is real and is answered rather than ignored: 2026081233 belongs to E11 wave 3, it is named here as a deliberate carry, and every E12 artifact that uses it records both experiments. The alternative — a fresh number — would forfeit the same-seed comparison the spec asks for, and would make w3-vs-A2w a two-variable read.
the_two_seed_rule: E10's closing ruling R3 binds here from birth: a scene observation from ONE seed is an observation, never a route property. Wave 2 runs both registered seeds on one arm, so a world claim that replicates across them is a claim about the arm; a claim that does not is an observation about a seed.

ceiling.note: SIX submissions total, amended 4 -> 6 by the Director on 2026-08-12 in the same exchange that restructured the arms. Wave 2 as originally amended was A1w x2 + A2w x2 = 4; at Gate LOOK the Director ruled A1w broken and approved A2w, so A1w's two are NOT spent and wave 2 costs 2. Wave 3 (catalog 6.0/uni_pc on the approved world, same two seeds) is 2 more. Projected total 4 of 6. estimate_credits is recorded before the first submission and both meters are reported; on an all-OSS graph it returns 0 by construction, so the ceiling is enforced by counting generations. Spent GPU time has no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
ceiling.why_machine_readable: The value was free prose and no tool under tools/ read the key, while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated. CLAUDE.md makes the credit ceiling a per-spec obligation and records that spent credits have no compensator, so the one unrecoverable resource in this repo was bounded by a string nothing could parse. The prose is not deleted: it is `note`, verbatim, and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it. CORRECTION, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 8, F-6c5c537b). This paragraph used to argue the fix with the clause “while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated”, and to close “and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it”. Both halves were measured on the tree and only one survived. `grep -rn allocation tools/ --include=*.py` returns 0 hits: `allocation` has no reader at all, so it is exactly as unread as `ceiling` was when it was filed. `seeds` has seven readers — build_animate_payload.py:487 (main), build_camera_i2v_payload.py:1182 (main), build_i2v_payload.py:793 (main), build_lora_arm_payload.py:467 (gate_s), build_r2v_payload.py:324 (build_and_write), build_t2v_payload.py:498 (main) and gate_saved_graph.py:1054 (main) — each handing the list to a seed gate, so that half of the claim holds. And no tool reads `ceiling` from a seeds spec either: every `ceiling` hit under tools/ is `armature_core.assembly`'s unrelated CASCADE slot ceiling, or a builder passing that one. So `ceiling.submissions` is a number a submission step COULD count against and none does today — the bound is held by the spec and the executor, not by code. The original claim is kept above rather than deleted, because the correction is more useful than the original. tests/test_seeds_specs.py pins the measurement; the day a builder counts against `ceiling.submissions`, that test flips with it and this paragraph is rewritten again. binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. armature_core/gates.py::gate_s_seed_registration enforces both clauses at build time and armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces them again against the saved file the cloud actually executes.
the_inert_second_seed: The low-noise expert's KSamplerAdvanced carries noise_seed 0 with add_noise=disable. It draws nothing, so it is inert; route_gates.gate_s_registration reports it and does not demand it be registered. Recorded here so a reader of the graph does not find an unregistered 0 and take it for a gap in this list.
